title: Execution Security (Grimdall)
markdown:
Grimdall is an **optional** execution-security layer for the tool-use boundary. Because RAG context and inbound channel messages (email, Slack, Telegram, Discord, Google Chat) are injected into user turns, a malicious document or message can steer the model into tool calls that exfiltrate secrets, destroy state, or burn unbounded LLM spend. Grimdall adds deterministic, sub-millisecond pre-execution checks so the model's judgment is not the only line of defense.

### Controls
Every skill / MCP tool call is evaluated at the dispatch boundary in `orchestrator/executive.py` (and re-checked at `MCPGateway.call_tool`, covering direct callers like the scheduler) against four rules:

1. **Secret denial** — blocks arguments that name credential paths (`.env`, `~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, `company/`, `/data`, Google service-account JSON, `episodic_memory.db`, `chroma_db`).
2. **Egress allowlist** — bare `http(s)` URL arguments must resolve to an allowlisted host, matched exactly or as a real subdomain; fails closed. Public-fetch tools (`web_search`, `scrape_url`, `load_mcp_server`) are exempt because their data path terminates at allowlisted providers.
3. **Destructive block** — blocks shell-destructive fragments in arguments (`rm -rf`, `sudo`, `chmod 777`, `shutdown`, `git reset --hard`, `DROP` / `TRUNCATE TABLE`). There is deliberately no tool-name denylist: legitimate delete tools (`delete_skill`, `remove_watchlist_entry`) must keep working.
4. **Per-session spend guardrail** — sums the session's `cache_event` audit rows (the same numbers the /audit usage view shows) and blocks further dispatch once `GRIMDALL_MAX_TOKENS_PER_SESSION` or `GRIMDALL_MAX_COST_USD_PER_SESSION` is exceeded, catching runaway opus extended-thinking loops that recur across turns.

### Deployment modes
`GRIMDALL_ENABLED=false` (default) makes the guard a no-op — a fresh checkout behaves identically. `GRIMDALL_ENABLED=true` switches to Shadow Mode: violations are written to the existing `audit_log` as signed `grimdall_block` receipts and execution proceeds. Adding `GRIMDALL_ENFORCE=true` switches to Enforce Mode: violating calls return an error `tool_result` the model can react to.

### Receipts
Every block writes an HMAC-SHA256-signed receipt (key: `GRIMDALL_SIGNING_KEY` env var, or an auto-generated owner-only `company/.grimdall-key`) into the audit trail, so a tampered log is detectable. Guard checks are deterministic string/ledger checks only — no LLM calls, no network, no shell — and audit writes swallow exceptions, so a guard failure never breaks a turn.
